review_notes: Read the whole file and grepped the EGZ sources for competing point-mapping definitions. Mathlib was not searched for a counterpart to `RationalPolytope.Face.preimage`; it is a library-specific structure, so I did not check. `SupHom`, `Finset.sup'` and affine-map lemmas are already used. The one concrete duplication is internal: `ConvexFlag.Point.map` versus `SubdivisionMap.point`, plus the inlined constructor in `proper`. The two definitions are definitionally equal by inspection. I did not check uses outside this file. Confidence is moderate, because the rubric's focus is on competing versions of Mathlib concepts and this duplication is internal to the library.

findings.excerpt:
def point (q : Ψ.flag.Point) : Φ.flag.Point :=
  ⟨M.node q.base, M.fibre q.base q.val, M.polytope_mem q.base q.val_mem⟩
findings.problem: The same file defines the induced map on flag points twice, as independent declarations. `ConvexFlag.Point.map` (line 32) builds `⟨node q.base, fibre q.base q.val, hpolytope q.base q.val_mem⟩`. `SubdivisionMap.point` rebuilds the identical anonymous constructor from the structure fields. The `proper` field (line 171) spells the constructor out a third time, because `point` cannot be used inside its own structure declaration. As a result `ofLocalGenerators` and `ConvexCombination.map` talk about `Point.map`, while `point_coord`, `comp_point` and `point_mem_pointsOnFace` talk about `point`. The two coincide only by definitional unfolding, and nothing states this.
findings.proposed_change: Define `SubdivisionMap.point q := q.map M.node M.fibre M.polytope_mem`, so there is one implementation. Optionally add a `point_eq_map` lemma, which holds by `rfl`. Likewise state `proper` using `Point.map`, as `q.map node fibre polytope_mem ∈ Φ.omega`. This matches the form `hgenerators` already uses in `ofLocalGenerators`. Keep the name `point` as a named specialisation.
findings.benefit: There is a single definition of the point-mapping operation. The `proper` field and the `ofLocalGenerators` hypothesis use the same expression, so no conversion between two spellings is needed, and any change to the point construction has one place to edit.
